actions.justification: Patient presents with bilateral leg edema and weight gain — assess volume status first to confirm wet/warm profile and guide diuretic dosing.
Critical to classify hemodynamic profile (wet/warm vs wet/cold) before initiating treatment. BP 135/82 and HR 80 suggest adequate perfusion, but must confirm to avoid inappropriate inotrope use.
BNP or NT-proBNP is essential to confirm acute decompensated HF, quantify severity, and provide a baseline for monitoring treatment response.
BMP is critical to assess renal function (CKD stage 3), electrolytes (K+, Na+), and BUN/creatinine before and during IV diuretic therapy. NSAID use may have further worsened renal function.
Chest X-ray is essential to assess for pulmonary edema, pleural effusions, and cardiomegaly in this acute decompensated HF presentation.

Patient is wet/warm (congested with adequate perfusion). IV furosemide is the first-line treatment for acute decompensated HFrEF with volume overload. Guideline-directed for congested, well-perfused profile. Inotropes are contraindicated in this warm/wet scenario.
Echocardiogram is essential to assess ejection fraction, wall motion abnormalities, and confirm HFrEF diagnosis per AHA guidelines. Will guide GDMT initiation and assess severity of decompensation.
Troponin should be ordered to rule out acute coronary syndrome as a precipitant of this decompensated HF episode. Patient's decompensation may have an ischemic trigger.

Cardiology consultation is indicated for HFrEF decompensation management, optimization of GDMT (ACE/ARB/ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i), and to address NSAID discontinuation (ibuprofen is contraindicated in HF and contributing to fluid retention/CKD progression).

Patient is WET and WARM (BP 135/82, SpO2 96%, adequate perfusion) with volume overload. Vasodilators (e.g., nitroglycerin) can reduce preload and afterload in this hemodynamically stable congested HFrEF patient, complementing the IV diuretic already given. This is appropriate for the warm-wet profile per AHA HF guidelines.

Patient has HFrEF with acute decompensation. While current presentation appears warm and wet (MAP 100, SpO2 96%), echocardiogram is pending and perfusion status could deteriorate. This optional action is appropriate to prepare for potential cardiogenic/cold-wet profile if echo reveals severely reduced EF or if clinical status worsens. It is the only available action remaining and monitoring for cardiogenic shock readiness is clinically prudent given HFrEF diagnosis.

Mandatory action: obtain detailed history including duration of symptoms, NSAID use (ibuprofen - contraindicated in HFrEF), fluid intake, and medication compliance. Critical given patient is taking OTC ibuprofen which worsens HF.
Mandatory action: perform full physical examination including assessment of JVD, S3 gallop, crackles, peripheral edema severity to characterize hemodynamic profile (warm/wet vs cold/wet).
Mandatory action: patient has CKD stage 3 and is on NSAIDs - renal function and electrolytes are critical to guide diuretic dosing and safety. Also needed before initiating GDMT.

Mandatory: BNP/NT-proBNP is required to confirm acute decompensated HF and guide management. Note: order_lab_bnp was completed but order_bnp_or_ntprobnp is a distinct required mandatory action in this phase.
Mandatory: CBC required to evaluate for anemia (common HF precipitant) and baseline hematologic status. Patient has CKD stage 3 increasing risk of anemia.

Mandatory: Chest X-ray needed to assess for pulmonary edema and degree of fluid overload in this patient with bilateral leg edema and worsening congestion. Prior CXR order_imaging_cxr was completed but order_chest_xray is listed as a distinct mandatory action.

MANDATORY action - ECG is required in HFrEF workup to assess for arrhythmias, ischemia, and conduction abnormalities that may be contributing to decompensation. Also needed prior to considering ICD/CRT candidacy.
MANDATORY action - TSH is required to rule out thyroid dysfunction (hypothyroidism or hyperthyroidism) as a reversible cause or exacerbating factor of HFrEF.

Patient appears 'wet and warm' (congested with adequate perfusion: BP 135/82, SpO2 96%), but formal hemodynamic profile assessment is needed to guide further therapy including diuresis intensity and potential vasodilator therapy. This also informs safe GDMT initiation.

LVEF assessment is essential to confirm HFrEF diagnosis, quantify degree of systolic dysfunction, and guide GDMT initiation (ACE/ARB/ARNI, beta-blocker, MRA, SGLT2i). Echo was ordered but LVEF needs formal documentation.
Per AHA guidelines, ICD implantation is strongly recommended for eligible HFrEF patients after GDMT optimization. Assess candidacy now to plan device therapy appropriately.
CRT should be assessed in HFrEF patients with reduced EF, particularly if there is evidence of bundle branch block or dyssynchrony on ECG, as it can improve outcomes.
Guideline requires documenting NYHA class for HFrEF classification. This has not been completed yet and is required per AHA guidelines to guide management decisions.

violation_events.description: Action order_bnp_or_ntprobnp performed 10 min after deadline
Action outside allowed set without justification: order_lab_cbc
Action obtain_12_lead_ecg performed 25 min after deadline
